headline: Every major sits under its 200-day line while short sellers keep getting run over: a market that's technically bearish but positioned the other way
paragraphs: Start with the trend map, because it's unanimous in a way that's rare: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day moving averages, and none show a golden cross. That's seven for seven on the bearish side of the long-term trend gauge, even though the short-term tape looks constructive almost everywhere. BTC is up 0.27% on the day, up 0.48% over seven days, and up 8.57% over thirty days, sitting 47.8% below its twelve-month high of $124,739.81. ETH is flat-to-up on the day (+0.30%) and the week (+0.13%) but has added 22.22% over thirty days while still 60.1% off its high. ADA is the standout: down 0.45% today but up 16.76% over the week and 36.77% over the month, though it remains 79.4% below its twelve-month peak. The pattern across the board is the same: real 30-day gains layered on top of a still-broken long-term structure.

Momentum tells a mixed story against that backdrop. RSI readings cluster in the mid-50s to mid-60s (BTC 55.6, ETH 57.3, SOL 58.0, BNB 66.1, ADA 67.4), which is constructive without being stretched, but XRP's 41.2 and DOGE's 45.6 sit below neutral even as both post 24h gains. The more interesting split is in MACD: ETH's MACD line sits below its signal despite the asset's 22.22% 30-day advance, a momentum lag worth naming rather than a red flag on its own. XRP shows the same bearish MACD alongside a weak RSI, consistent with its -3.79% seven-day and roughly flat 30-day (-0.29%) performance. DOGE is the odd one: MACD reads bullish even as price is down 0.18% over the week and 5.29% over the month, a genuine momentum-versus-price divergence.

Positioning is where the tension sharpens. Funding is positive across the board, meaning longs are paying shorts to hold their bets: BTC at 9.6% annualized, ETH a mild 2.8%, SOL and DOGE both near 10%, and XRP the richest at 11.0%. Long/short account ratios show the crowd leaning hard into that side, especially in the smaller names: DOGE at 4.99 longs per short, XRP at 3.61, SOL at 2.01, versus a much more balanced BTC at 1.14. Yet look at who's actually getting liquidated. Over the past 21 to 23 hours, BTC shorts lost $636,350 versus just $140,635 in longs; ETH shorts lost $2.69 million versus $182,476 in longs; SOL shorts lost $878,345 versus $81,351 in longs. Shorts are the ones getting squeezed on the majors even as funding says longs are the crowded, paying side. XRP and DOGE flip that: longs took the bigger liquidation hit ($327,179 vs $28,488 for XRP; $134,275 vs $4,368 for DOGE), which lines up with their softer price action.

On flows, the traditional-finance bid keeps showing up. The BTC spot ETF posted $101.7 million net on 07 Aug 2026, part of a $865.3 million five-session net with five consecutive same-direction days, a genuine short trend of accumulation by that measure. ETH's ETF added $49.6 million on the same date, with $243.7 million over five sessions and four same-direction days, a softer but still positive read. Stablecoin float sits at $306.24 billion, down 1.02% over the past 30 days, so the dry powder on the sidelines has actually contracted slightly even as ETF buying continued. Whale wallets moved $103,045,101 net off exchanges in the last 48 hours, driven by two large BTC withdrawals from Kraken ($117.99 million and $50.07 million) against a $65.01 million deposit into Binance. The trailing four weekly readings were -$86.7 million, +$385.7 million, +$1,075.3 million, and +$67.2 million: three of the last four weeks net left exchanges, though this week's pace is the lightest of the outflow weeks.

Sentiment sits at 31, labeled Fear, near the top of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. That's a crowd still nervous by the gauge's own history even as ETF flows stay positive, shorts keep getting liquidated on the majors, and coins keep trickling off exchanges. The disagreement between what the sentiment index says and what positioning and flows are doing is the notable thing here, not a resolution either way. Worth watching from here: whether BTC or any major reclaims its 200-day average, whether funding flips negative as a sign the long crowd is unwinding, and whether the ETF five-session net or the weekly whale flow series changes direction. Any of those would tell you the picture actually shifted, rather than just bounced.
